includedPullRequests.title: Fix duration translations and unify duration formatting
includedPullRequests.body:
This unifies duration and time ago formatting so pod, sensor, loop, glucose age, overrides and temp targets use the same format and follow the user's locale, e.g. "1h 30m" in English and "1h 30min" in French.

- VoiceOver should now read durations in the user's language and with correct plurals. Most of these strings were still in English for other languages
- VoiceOver reads "1h 30m" as "1 hour, 30 minutes" instead of "meters"
- Pod time keeps the minutes past 12 hours ("14h 30m" instead of "14h"). I wasn't sure if dropping them was intentional, happy to bring it back if it was
- Removed `TimeAgoFormatter` and a few duration helpers that did the same thing
- Added tests

No new translations, only marked unused ones as stale

includedPullRequests.title: Fix Medtrum crash loop and device delete races
includedPullRequests.body:
MedtrumKit sent alert pump events from a background task instead of Trio's pump queue, so reservoir empty, occlusion, fault, max-limit and base-reset alarms crashed Trio. Because the alarm fired again on every launch, the app crash-looped.

- MedtrumKit: send the pump event on the delegate queue again
   - Reported by @LiroyvH via DM. PR based on provided crash report.
- SyaiKit, LibreLoop: run `delete()` on the main actor to fix data races from async deletion
- Trio: set the pump's delegate queue before its delegate

includedPullRequests.title: Wait for first unlock before opening Core Data
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

After an iPhone restart, iOS can launch Trio in the background (Bluetooth, background refresh) before the user unlocks the phone for the first time. Until that first unlock, every protected file is unreadable, so loading `TrioCoreDataPersistentContainer.sqlite` fails with `NSSQLiteErrorDomain=23` (authorization denied).

`CoreDataStack` retried three times about a second apart, then gave up for good. Trio stayed on **"Oops, something went wrong"** and did not loop until the user opened it and force-quit it. Seen on device on 25 Oct:

```
15:16:19 Trio started
15:16:20 Loading persistent stores failed: Code=256 … NSSQLiteErrorDomain=23
15:16:49 Core Data initialization failed after 3 attempts
(no looping until the app was force-quit and reopened at 15:23)
```

## Change

- `CoreDataStack.initializeStack` now waits for `UIApplication.protectedDataDidBecomeAvailableNotification` before loading the store, when protected data isn't available yet. When it is (every normal launch), nothing changes.
- The wait re-checks availability after adding its observer, so an unlock in between is not missed, and it resumes exactly once.
- In-memory stacks (tests, previews) skip the wait.
- Trio can't be opened before the first unlock, so the wait only happens during a background launch and is invisible to users.

Pump and CGM state files are protected the same way, so Trio could not loop before the first unlock anyway. The difference is that it now starts by itself once the phone is unlocked, instead of failing permanently.

## Testing

- New `CoreDataProtectedDataTests` (3 tests): returns at once when available, waits for the notification, and catches an unlock during the check.
- `GlucoseStorage Tests` and `JSON Importer Tests` pass on the same run. SwiftFormat build is clean.
- Tested in-vivo on iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 26.6.1 running latest dev + this change, Medtrum Nano and G7 direct.

includedPullRequests.title: fix(food-camera): Rotate by each camera's mount so iPhone Duo's inner camera is upright
includedPullRequests.body:
On iPhone Duo with the phone open, the food camera's preview and photo came out turned 90°. The camera picked its angle from the screen orientation, which assumes every camera sits like a classic iPhone's. It now takes the angle from `AVCaptureDevice.RotationCoordinator`, which knows each camera's mount. The photo is now cropped to the scan frame before it's turned upright, because the crop rectangle and the stored pixels are both in the sensor's unrotated coordinates.

Tested: the new `FoodCameraCropTests` pass on the iOS 27.2 simulator. Not yet checked on a physical Duo.
